nodes.title: Running slop on a repo
nodes.sub: One command: index, check, serve, open
nodes.detail: `slop` in a repo that has a story re-reads the code, checks the story against it, starts the app on 127.0.0.1 and opens the browser. Without a story it stops and points at /slop-map.

nodes.title: The map
nodes.sub: The surface cards on an infinite whiteboard
nodes.detail: The roots of the story, laid out in one readable line with labelled wires, on a board you can drag and zoom. Clicking a card glides it to the top left and opens its level.

nodes.title: A card, opened
nodes.sub: The trail, the level below, and the pane
nodes.detail: The trail on the left says where you are; under it, the cards one level down; on the right, the detail pane for the open card. Every move is a URL, so the mouse's back button walks back through cards.

nodes.title: The code pane
nodes.sub: Editable code for the open card, drillable by calls
nodes.detail: The open card's code units, one after another, each with an editable signature and body. A unit's calls and a class's methods open as a deeper list inside the pane rather than as new levels.

nodes.title: .slop/story.json
nodes.detail: Cards, flows, edges and links. Code is named only by symbol id, never quoted, so the story survives the code moving around. Written by the /slop-map skill and committed.

nodes.title: The index
nodes.sub: Every function, class and method, read fresh
nodes.detail: Rebuilt from the code on every map load, so line numbers and bodies are never stale. `slop index` also writes it to .slop/index.json, which stays out of git.

nodes.title: The repo's files
nodes.sub: Where a saved card is written

nodes.title: Starting up
nodes.sub: Refuses to serve a story with errors

rows.title: Needs a story
rows.detail: No .slop/story.json: exit, and say to run /slop-map.

rows.title: Index the code
rows.detail: Writes .slop/index.json, and a .gitignore beside it the first time.

rows.title: Check the story
rows.detail: Errors stop the run; warnings (drift) are printed and the map still opens.

rows.title: Build if stale
rows.detail: Rebuilds the Next app when any source under ui/ is newer than the last build.

rows.title: Serve on 127.0.0.1
rows.detail: next start on a free port from 4747, with SLOP_REPO set; opens the browser once it answers.

nodes.title: Moving around the board
nodes.detail: The camera is three motion values written straight to the DOM. React never re-renders while you drag, which is what keeps the cards from lagging behind the pointer.

rows.label: Drag
rows.value: pans; a drag that starts on a card doesn't open it

rows.label: Wheel
rows.value: pans; ctrl or ⌘ + wheel zooms at the pointer, 25%–250%

rows.label: Fit
rows.value: until you move, the map refits to the window on resize

nodes.title: Laying out the roots
nodes.sub: One line in edge order, stores to the side

nodes.title: Back and forward
nodes.detail: The open path lives in the URL (?map=…&at=a/b). A move pushes a history entry and popstate restores one, so browser back, the mouse's side buttons and swipes step through cards. Plain clicks are taken over; middle and ctrl clicks are left to the browser.

rows.title: Path → URL
rows.detail: pushState on every move; the first sync only replaces, so landing leaves no extra step.

rows.title: URL → path
rows.detail: On popstate, the longest prefix of the URL's path that still resolves.

nodes.title: Drilling into calls
nodes.sub: A stack inside the pane, not new levels

nodes.title: Saving an edit
nodes.sub: Refuses if the file changed underneath
nodes.detail: An edit remembers the code it started from. Saving sends that along; the server finds the unit by id in the file as it is now and writes only if it still reads the same. Then the whole map is re-read, so every line number after the edit moves too.

rows.title: Edit in the card
rows.detail: Held in memory per card, with the body it started from.

rows.title: Save or Ctrl+S
rows.detail: POST /api/save with the symbol id, the starting body and the new one.

rows.title: Compare on disk
rows.detail: The unit is re-read from its file by id. Different from the starting body: 409, nothing written.

rows.title: Write
rows.detail: The unit's lines are replaced, through a temp file and a rename.

rows.title: Re-read the map
rows.detail: The edit is dropped only after the fresh map is in, so the card never flashes the old code.

anatomy.at: if (now.body !== before) throw new SaveConflict(`${symbol} changed on disk since it was loaded`);
anatomy.why: The whole conflict rule: compare text, not line numbers, so a shifted function still saves and a changed one never gets overwritten.

code.sub: Finds the unit by id, compares, writes
Only the page this server serves may read or write

nodes.title: Story + index → the map
nodes.sub: Missing code is a warning, not a failure
nodes.detail: The server merges the story with a fresh index and resolves anchored quotes against the files. The loader then checks it in two passes. Schema and broken references fail with a list of problems; code the story names that no longer exists becomes a partial, alarmed card that says what is gone.

rows.title: Merge
rows.detail: Anchors (file + first line) become snippets; an anchor that matches twice is a warning.

rows.title: Schema
rows.detail: zod: every field, every block kind.

rows.title: References
rows.detail: Unique ids, real parents, sibling edges, links to real rows.

rows.title: Build the tree
rows.detail: Code refs become code cards; a class's methods become its children; calls resolve to cards.

nodes.title: Reading the code
nodes.sub: TypeScript's own parser, TS and JS only
nodes.detail: Every TS/JS file git knows about is parsed with the TypeScript compiler. Units get ids from their names, never their lines. Calls are resolved through the type checker, falling back to a same-file name match. Rust, Python and the rest are not indexed: a story can still quote them with an anchored source block.
